And Abdullah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Ibn Shadhan informed us, from Ja'unah ibn Muhammad, saying: Salih ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Sulayman ibn Amr, from Ibn Hazm, from Anas ibn Malik, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Every night a caller calls out: 'Build for death!' and a caller calls out: 'Build for ruin!' A caller calls out: 'O Allah, give the one who spends a replacement!' and a caller calls out: 'O Allah, give the one who withholds destruction!' A caller calls out: 'Would that people had not been created!' and a caller calls out: 'Would that, when they were created, they had reflected on what they were created for!'" [Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 8/222.]

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Hafiz informed me, saying: Musa ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn Alawiyyah narrated to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Isa narrated to us, saying: al-Musayyib narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Abd al-Rahman, from his father, who said: Umar said to Suhayb: "You are a man who does not hold back anything." He said: "I heard Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, say: 'Whatever you spend of anything, He will replace it.'"

"And He is the best of providers."

Abu Sufyan al-Thaqafi informed me, saying: al-Fadl ibn al-Fadl al-Kindi narrated to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn Dawud al-Khashshab narrated to us, saying: Suwayd ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Hamid ibn al-Hasan narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Every act of goodness is charity. What a man spends on himself and his family is charity for him. What he uses to protect his honour is charity. And whatever a believer spends, its replacement is guaranteed by Allah, except what is spent on building or in disobedience." [Nasb al-Rayah: 4/415.]

Abd al-Hamid said: I asked Muhammad: "What is the meaning of 'what a man uses to protect his honour'?" He said: "Giving to a poet, or to one whose tongue is feared."

Mujahid said: If there is something in the hand of one of you, let him be moderate, and let him not interpret this verse, "Whatever you spend of anything, He will replace it," as a license, for provision is apportioned; perhaps his provision is little while he spends as one who is wealthy. The meaning of the verse is: "Whatever is from a replacement, it is from Him." A person may spend all his wealth in good, and then remain in need until he dies; but whatever replacement there is, it is from Him. The evidence for Mujahid's interpretation is what:

Abu Sufyan al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Bushayr narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Abi al-Khusayb informed me, saying: Mu'adh ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Amr ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ibn Allanah, that is Muhammad, narrated to us, from al-Awza'i, from Ibn Abi Musa, from Abu Umamah, who said: "You interpret this verse other than its true interpretation: 'Whatever you spend of anything, He will replace it.'"

And I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say, and otherwise may I be silent: "Beware of extravagance in wealth and spending, and hold to moderation, for no people ever became poor who were moderate."

And he (peace be upon him) said: "No one who is moderate ever suffered want." [Musnad Ahmad: 1/447.]

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Musa ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim al-Baghawi narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Hanbal narrated to us, saying: Asim ibn Khalid narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr informed me, saying: Hamzah narrated to us, from Abu al-Darda', from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Part of a man's understanding is gentleness in his livelihood." [Majma' al-Zawa'id: 4/74.]

"And He is the best of providers." The use of the plural (al-raziqin) is permissible because it is said: "The sultan provides for (razaqa) the soldiers," and "So-and-so provides for his dependents," as if He said: "He is the best of those who give."

"And on the Day when He gathers them all together, He will say to the angels: 'Did these people used to worship you?'" That is, these disbelievers. The angels will then disown them and say: "Glory be to You (subhanaka): exalted are You. You are our Protector, not them. Rather, they used to worship the jinn," that is, they obeyed Iblis, his offspring and his helpers in disobedience to You. "Most of them believed in them," that is, they were believers in them.

Qatadah said: It is an interrogative, its meaning like His saying to Jesus: "Did you say to the people, 'Take me and my mother as two gods besides God?'" (al-Ma'idah: 116).

"So today none of you will have power to benefit or harm another," whether intercession or punishment. "And We will say to those who did wrong: 'Taste the punishment of the Fire which you used to deny' in the world, for you have now come to it."

"And when Our clear verses are recited to them, they say: 'This is nothing but a man who wants to turn you away from what your fathers used to worship.'" That is, Muhammad (ﷺ). "And they say: 'This is nothing but a fabricated lie,'" meaning the Qur'an. "And those who disbelieved said of the truth when it came to them: 'This is nothing but clear magic.'"

"We did not give them (these polytheists) any books which they study," that is, which they read, "nor did We send to them any warner before you." "And those before them denied (Our messengers and Our revelation), and these (polytheists) have not attained even a tenth of what We gave them" (that is, the deniers of the earlier nations, in strength, blessing and long life). "So they denied My messengers, and how was My rejection!" Meaning My disapproval and My change against them. He warns the disbelievers of this community of the punishment of the earlier nations.

His words, exalted is He: "Say: I only exhort you (a'izukum: I command and advise you) to one thing," one single matter, which is: "that you stand up for God," for the sake of Allah. The "an" here is in the genitive position as an explanation of "wahidah," and its rendering is: "two by two" (mathna), meaning two at a time, pairing with one another, "and singly" (furada), one by one, reflecting, "then you reflect together." Reflection (al-fikr) is seeking meaning with the heart, so that you may know: "there is no madness (jinnah) in your companion Muhammad," as you claim; "ma" here is a negation and denial. "He is only a warner to you before a severe punishment."

"Say: Whatever reward I have asked of you for conveying the message and giving counsel, it is for you. My reward is only from God," that is, my recompense is only from Allah. "And He is over all things a witness." "Say: Indeed my Lord hurls (yaqdhifu: casts and brings) the truth, sending it down from heaven to the best of the prophets, the Knower of the unseen (allam al-ghuyub)," in the nominative as the predicate of "inna."

It has also been said: its meaning is "restraining (kaff) people," that is, it restrains them from the disbelief they are upon and calls them to Islam, and the ha' in it is for emphasis (intensification).

"...as a bearer of good news and a warner, but most people do not know. And they say: When will this promise be, if you are truthful? Say: For you is the appointment of a Day from which you cannot delay an hour nor advance it." And those who disbelieved said: "We will never believe in this Qur'an or in what came before it of the Scriptures." Then He described their state in their final outcome, saying: "If only you could see when the wrongdoers (al-zalimun: the disbelievers) are made to stand before their Lord, sending back the word to one another. Those who were deemed weak will say to those who were arrogant: 'Were it not for you, we would have been believers.' Those who were arrogant will say to those who were deemed weak: 'Did we turn you away from guidance after it came to you? Rather, you were criminals.'" And those who were deemed weak will say to those who were arrogant: "Rather, it was your scheming by night and day," that is, your scheming against us. The two are like the saying: "The matter was resolved (ʿazama al-amr)," and "So-and-so's day is fasting and his night is standing (in prayer)."

The poet said:

"I slept, though the night of the travelling camels is not a sleeper's night."

It has also been said: the scheming of night and day against them is the long duration of safety in them, like His saying: "So the term seemed long to them" (al-Hadid: 16), and similar.

"...when you were ordering us to disbelieve in God and set up rivals to Him." And they concealed (asarru) the regret, and this is one of the words with opposite meanings (al-addaad), which can mean concealing and also displaying. "When they saw the punishment. We will place the shackles (al-aghlal: the collars of fire) around the necks of those who disbelieved, the followers and the followed. Are they recompensed except for what they used to do?" in the world?

"We never sent a warner (nadhir: a messenger) to a town but its affluent (mutrafun: its leaders and wealthy) said: 'We disbelieve in what you have been sent with.' And they said: 'We have more wealth and children than you, and we will not be punished.'" Had He not been pleased with the religion and deeds we are upon, He would not have granted us wealth and children.

"Your wealth and your children are not what will bring you near to Us in position, except for those who believe" (but whoever believes) "and does righteous deeds, for them is the reward of double for what they did" (in reward, a single good deed being multiplied tenfold). The reading of the majority is "al-ghurafat" in the plural, and Abu Ubayd preferred it, saying: because of His saying: "We will surely settle them in lofty chambers (ghurafan) of Paradise" (al-Ankabut: 58). Al-A'mash and Hamzah read "fi al-ghurfah" in the singular.

"And those who strive (yas'awna): they work against Our verses, seeking to nullify Our proofs and Our Book, and (mu'ajizin: as opponents, obstinate ones), thinking that they can escape Us by themselves and outpace Us. Al-Kalbi said: whatever charity you give and whatever you spend in goodness and piety, "He will replace it," either by hastening it to you in this world or by storing it up for you in the Hereafter.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn informed me, saying: Ahmad ibn Ja'far ibn Hamdan ibn Abdullah narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Dawud al-Qantari narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: al-Layth ibn Sa'd narrated to us, from Amr ibn al-Harith, from Abu Yunus, mawla of Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of God (ﷺ), that he said: "Indeed, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said to me: 'Spend, and I will spend upon you.'" [Fath al-Bari: 9/411; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 6/240.]

And Abdullah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Ibn Shadhan informed us, from Ja'unah ibn Muhammad, saying: Salih ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Sulayman ibn Amr, from Ibn Hazm, from Anas ibn Malik, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Every night a caller calls out: 'Build for death!' and a caller calls out: 'Build for ruin!' A caller calls out: 'O Allah, give the one who spends a replacement!' and a caller calls out: 'O Allah, give the one who withholds destruction!' A caller calls out: 'Would that people had not been created!' and a caller calls out: 'Would that, when they were created, they had reflected on what they were created for!'" [Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 8/222.]

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Hafiz informed me, saying: Musa ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn Alawiyyah narrated to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Isa narrated to us, saying: al-Musayyib narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Abd al-Rahman, from his father, who said: Umar said to Suhayb: "You are a man who does not hold back anything." He said: "I heard Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, say: 'Whatever you spend of anything, He will replace it.'"

Abdullah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far informed us, saying: Ali ibn Harb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad narrated to us from Mujahid and Miqsam, from Ibn Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "I have been given five things, and I say this not out of boasting: I was sent to the red and the black (of mankind); the earth has been made for me a purifier and a place of prostration; spoils of war have been made lawful for me, which were not lawful for anyone before me; I was aided by terror, which marches before me the distance of a month's journey; and I have been given intercession, which I have stored up for my community on the Day of Resurrection, and it will, God willing, reach whoever did not associate anything with God."

It has also been said: its meaning is "restraining (kaff) people," that is, it restrains them from the disbelief they are upon and calls them to Islam, and the ha' in it is for emphasis (intensification).

"...as a bearer of good news and a warner, but most people do not know. And they say: When will this promise be, if you are truthful? Say: For you is the appointment of a Day from which you cannot delay an hour nor advance it." And those who disbelieved said: "We will never believe in this Qur'an or in what came before it of the Scriptures." Then He described their state in their final outcome, saying: "If only you could see when the wrongdoers (al-zalimun: the disbelievers) are made to stand before their Lord, sending back the word to one another. Those who were deemed weak will say to those who were arrogant: 'Were it not for you, we would have been believers.' Those who were arrogant will say to those who were deemed weak: 'Did we turn you away from guidance after it came to you? Rather, you were criminals.'" And those who were deemed weak will say to those who were arrogant: "Rather, it was your scheming by night and day," that is, your scheming against us. The two are like the saying: "The matter was resolved (ʿazama al-amr)," and "So-and-so's day is fasting and his night is standing (in prayer)."

The poet said:

"I slept, though the night of the travelling camels is not a sleeper's night."

It has also been said: the scheming of night and day against them is the long duration of safety in them, like His saying: "So the term seemed long to them" (al-Hadid: 16), and similar.

"...when you were ordering us to disbelieve in God and set up rivals to Him." And they concealed (asarru) the regret, and this is one of the words with opposite meanings (al-addaad), which can mean concealing and also displaying. "When they saw the punishment. We will place the shackles (al-aghlal: the collars of fire) around the necks of those who disbelieved, the followers and the followed. Are they recompensed except for what they used to do?" in the world?

"We never sent a warner (nadhir: a messenger) to a town but its affluent (mutrafun: its leaders and wealthy) said: 'We disbelieve in what you have been sent with.' And they said: 'We have more wealth and children than you, and we will not be punished.'" Had He not been pleased with the religion and deeds we are upon, He would not have granted us wealth and children.

"Say: Indeed my Lord extends provision to whom He wills and restricts it. But most people do not know," that such is the case.

"Your wealth and your children are not what will bring you near to Us in position, except for those who believe" (but whoever believes) "and does righteous deeds, for them is the reward of double for what they did" (in reward, a single good deed being multiplied tenfold). The word "man" (in illa man amana) may have two readings: one, that it is in the accusative as the object of "tuqarribukum" (brings you near); the other, that it is in the nominative, its meaning being: "It is nothing but those who believe." "And they will be in the upper chambers (al-ghurafat: the lofty stations), secure."

The reading of the majority is "jaza'u al-di'f" with the genitive construction. Ya'qub read "jaza'an" in the accusative and with tanwin. "Al-dif" is in the nominative, and its sense is: "So for them is double (al-dif) as a reward," through inversion of the order. The reading of the majority is "al-ghurafat" in the plural, and Abu Ubayd preferred it, saying: because of His saying: "We will surely settle them in lofty chambers (ghurafan) of Paradise" (al-Ankabut: 58). Al-A'mash and Hamzah read "fi al-ghurfah" in the singular.

"And those who strive (yas'awna): they work against Our verses, seeking to nullify Our proofs and Our Book, and (mu'ajizin: as opponents, obstinate ones), thinking that they can escape Us by themselves and outpace Us. Those will be brought forth to the punishment." Say: "Indeed my Lord extends provision to whom He wills of His servants and restricts it for him. And whatever you spend of anything, He will replace it." Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: what is spent without extravagance or stinginess, "He will replace it." Al-Kalbi said: whatever charity you give and whatever you spend in goodness and piety, "He will replace it," either by hastening it to you in this world or by storing it up for you in the Hereafter.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn informed me, saying: Ahmad ibn Ja'far ibn Hamdan ibn Abdullah narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Dawud al-Qantari narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: al-Layth ibn Sa'd narrated to us, from Amr ibn al-Harith, from Abu Yunus, mawla of Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of God (ﷺ), that he said: "Indeed, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said to me: 'Spend, and I will spend upon you.'" [Fath al-Bari: 9/411; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 6/240.]

And Abdullah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Ibn Shadhan informed us, from Ja'unah ibn Muhammad, saying: Salih ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Sulayman ibn Amr, from Ibn Hazm, from Anas ibn Malik, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Every night a caller calls out: 'Build for death!' and a caller calls out: 'Build for ruin!' A caller calls out: 'O Allah, give the one who spends a replacement!' and a caller calls out: 'O Allah, give the one who withholds destruction!' A caller calls out: 'Would that people had not been created!' and a caller calls out: 'Would that, when they were created, they had reflected on what they were created for!'" [Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 8/222.]

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Hafiz informed me, saying: Musa ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn Alawiyyah narrated to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Isa narrated to us, saying: al-Musayyib narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Abd al-Rahman, from his father, who said: Umar said to Suhayb: "You are a man who does not hold back anything." He said: "I heard Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, say: 'Whatever you spend of anything, He will replace it.'"

"And He is the best of providers."

Abu Sufyan al-Thaqafi informed me, saying: al-Fadl ibn al-Fadl al-Kindi narrated to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn Dawud al-Khashshab narrated to us, saying: Suwayd ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Hamid ibn al-Hasan narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Every act of goodness is charity. What a man spends on himself and his family is charity for him. What he uses to protect his honour is charity. And whatever a believer spends, its replacement is guaranteed by Allah, except what is spent on building or in disobedience." [Nasb al-Rayah: 4/415.]

Abd al-Hamid said: I asked Muhammad: "What is the meaning of 'what a man uses to protect his honour'?" He said: "Giving to a poet, or to one whose tongue is feared."

Mujahid said: If there is something in the hand of one of you, let him be moderate, and let him not interpret this verse, "Whatever you spend of anything, He will replace it," as a license, for provision is apportioned; perhaps his provision is little while he spends as one who is wealthy. The meaning of the verse is: "Whatever is from a replacement, it is from Him." A person may spend all his wealth in good, and then remain in need until he dies; but whatever replacement there is, it is from Him. The evidence for Mujahid's interpretation is what:

Abu Sufyan al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Bushayr narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Abi al-Khusayb informed me, saying: Mu'adh ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Amr ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ibn Allanah, that is Muhammad, narrated to us, from al-Awza'i, from Ibn Abi Musa, from Abu Umamah, who said: "You interpret this verse other than its true interpretation: 'Whatever you spend of anything, He will replace it.'"

And I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say, and otherwise may I be silent: "Beware of extravagance in wealth and spending, and hold to moderation, for no people ever became poor who were moderate."

And he (peace be upon him) said: "No one who is moderate ever suffered want." [Musnad Ahmad: 1/447.]

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Musa ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim al-Baghawi narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Hanbal narrated to us, saying: Asim ibn Khalid narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr informed me, saying: Hamzah narrated to us, from Abu al-Darda', from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Part of a man's understanding is gentleness in his livelihood." [Majma' al-Zawa'id: 4/74.]

"And He is the best of providers." The use of the plural (al-raziqin) is permissible because it is said: "The sultan provides for (razaqa) the soldiers," and "So-and-so provides for his dependents," as if He said: "He is the best of those who give."

"And on the Day when He gathers them all together, He will say to the angels: 'Did these people used to worship you?'" That is, these disbelievers. The angels will then disown them and say: "Glory be to You (subhanaka): exalted are You. You are our Protector, not them. Rather, they used to worship the jinn," that is, they obeyed Iblis, his offspring and his helpers in disobedience to You. "Most of them believed in them," that is, they were believers in them.

Qatadah said: It is an interrogative, its meaning like His saying to Jesus: "Did you say to the people, 'Take me and my mother as two gods besides God?'" (al-Ma'idah: 116).

"So today none of you will have power to benefit or harm another," whether intercession or punishment. "And We will say to those who did wrong: 'Taste the punishment of the Fire which you used to deny' in the world, for you have now come to it."

"And when Our clear verses are recited to them, they say: 'This is nothing but a man who wants to turn you away from what your fathers used to worship.'" That is, Muhammad (ﷺ). "And they say: 'This is nothing but a fabricated lie,'" meaning the Qur'an. "And those who disbelieved said of the truth when it came to them: 'This is nothing but clear magic.'"

"We did not give them (these polytheists) any books which they study," that is, which they read, "nor did We send to them any warner before you." "And those before them denied (Our messengers and Our revelation), and these (polytheists) have not attained even a tenth of what We gave them" (that is, the deniers of the earlier nations, in strength, blessing and long life). "So they denied My messengers, and how was My rejection!" Meaning My disapproval and My change against them. He warns the disbelievers of this community of the punishment of the earlier nations.

His words, exalted is He: "Say: I only exhort you (a'izukum: I command and advise you) to one thing," one single matter, which is: "that you stand up for God," for the sake of Allah. The "an" here is in the genitive position as an explanation of "wahidah," and its rendering is: "two by two" (mathna), meaning two at a time, pairing with one another, "and singly" (furada), one by one, reflecting, "then you reflect together." Reflection (al-fikr) is seeking meaning with the heart, so that you may know: "there is no madness (jinnah) in your companion Muhammad," as you claim; "ma" here is a negation and denial. "He is only a warner to you before a severe punishment."

"Say: Whatever reward I have asked of you for conveying the message and giving counsel, it is for you. My reward is only from God," that is, my recompense is only from Allah. "And He is over all things a witness." "Say: Indeed my Lord hurls (yaqdhifu: casts and brings) the truth, sending it down from heaven to the best of the prophets, the Knower of the unseen (allam al-ghuyub)," in the nominative as the predicate of "inna."

"So today none of you will have power to benefit or harm another," whether intercession or punishment. "And We will say to those who did wrong: 'Taste the punishment of the Fire which you used to deny' in the world, for you have now come to it."

"And when Our clear verses are recited to them, they say: 'This is nothing but a man who wants to turn you away from what your fathers used to worship.'" That is, Muhammad (ﷺ). "And they say: 'This is nothing but a fabricated lie,'" meaning the Qur'an. "And those who disbelieved said of the truth when it came to them: 'This is nothing but clear magic.'"

"We did not give them (these polytheists) any books which they study," that is, which they read, "nor did We send to them any warner before you." "And those before them denied (Our messengers and Our revelation), and these (polytheists) have not attained even a tenth of what We gave them" (that is, the deniers of the earlier nations, in strength, blessing and long life). "So they denied My messengers, and how was My rejection!" Meaning My disapproval and My change against them. He warns the disbelievers of this community of the punishment of the earlier nations.

His words, exalted is He: "Say: I only exhort you (a'izukum: I command and advise you) to one thing," one single matter, which is: "that you stand up for God," for the sake of Allah. The "an" here is in the genitive position as an explanation of "wahidah," and its rendering is: "two by two" (mathna), meaning two at a time, pairing with one another, "and singly" (furada), one by one, reflecting, "then you reflect together." Reflection (al-fikr) is seeking meaning with the heart, so that you may know: "there is no madness (jinnah) in your companion Muhammad," as you claim; "ma" here is a negation and denial. "He is only a warner to you before a severe punishment."

"Say: Whatever reward I have asked of you for conveying the message and giving counsel, it is for you. My reward is only from God," that is, my recompense is only from Allah. "And He is over all things a witness." "Say: Indeed my Lord hurls (yaqdhifu: casts and brings) the truth, sending it down from heaven to the best of the prophets, the Knower of the unseen (allam al-ghuyub)," in the nominative as the predicate of "inna."

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 34, verses 28–48:**

His words, may He be exalted: "We have not sent you except as a comprehensive messenger (kaffah) to all of mankind: the Arabs, the non-Arabs, and all the other nations."

Abdullah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far informed us, saying: Ali ibn Harb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad narrated to us from Mujahid and Miqsam, from Ibn Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "I have been given five things, and I say this not out of boasting: I was sent to the red and the black (of mankind); the earth has been made for me a purifier and a place of prostration; spoils of war have been made lawful for me, which were not lawful for anyone before me; I was aided by terror, which marches before me the distance of a month's journey; and I have been given intercession, which I have stored up for my community on the Day of Resurrection, and it will, God willing, reach whoever did not associate anything with God."

It has also been said: its meaning is "restraining (kaff) people," that is, it restrains them from the disbelief they are upon and calls them to Islam, and the ha' in it is for emphasis (intensification).

"...as a bearer of good news and a warner, but most people do not know. And they say: When will this promise be, if you are truthful? Say: For you is the appointment of a Day from which you cannot delay an hour nor advance it." And those who disbelieved said: "We will never believe in this Qur'an or in what came before it of the Scriptures." Then He described their state in their final outcome, saying: "If only you could see when the wrongdoers (al-zalimun: the disbelievers) are made to stand before their Lord, sending back the word to one another. Those who were deemed weak will say to those who were arrogant: 'Were it not for you, we would have been believers.' Those who were arrogant will say to those who were deemed weak: 'Did we turn you away from guidance after it came to you? Rather, you were criminals.'" And those who were deemed weak will say to those who were arrogant: "Rather, it was your scheming by night and day," that is, your scheming against us. The two are like the saying: "The matter was resolved (ʿazama al-amr)," and "So-and-so's day is fasting and his night is standing (in prayer)."

The poet said:

"I slept, though the night of the travelling camels is not a sleeper's night."

It has also been said: the scheming of night and day against them is the long duration of safety in them, like His saying: "So the term seemed long to them" (al-Hadid: 16), and similar.

"...when you were ordering us to disbelieve in God and set up rivals to Him." And they concealed (asarru) the regret, and this is one of the words with opposite meanings (al-addaad), which can mean concealing and also displaying. "When they saw the punishment. We will place the shackles (al-aghlal: the collars of fire) around the necks of those who disbelieved, the followers and the followed. Are they recompensed except for what they used to do?" in the world?

"We never sent a warner (nadhir: a messenger) to a town but its affluent (mutrafun: its leaders and wealthy) said: 'We disbelieve in what you have been sent with.' And they said: 'We have more wealth and children than you, and we will not be punished.'" Had He not been pleased with the religion and deeds we are upon, He would not have granted us wealth and children.

"Say: Indeed my Lord extends provision to whom He wills and restricts it. But most people do not know," that such is the case.

"Your wealth and your children are not what will bring you near to Us in position, except for those who believe" (but whoever believes) "and does righteous deeds, for them is the reward of double for what they did" (in reward, a single good deed being multiplied tenfold). The word "man" (in illa man amana) may have two readings: one, that it is in the accusative as the object of "tuqarribukum" (brings you near); the other, that it is in the nominative, its meaning being: "It is nothing but those who believe." "And they will be in the upper chambers (al-ghurafat: the lofty stations), secure."

The reading of the majority is "jaza'u al-di'f" with the genitive construction. Ya'qub read "jaza'an" in the accusative and with tanwin. "Al-dif" is in the nominative, and its sense is: "So for them is double (al-dif) as a reward," through inversion of the order. The reading of the majority is "al-ghurafat" in the plural, and Abu Ubayd preferred it, saying: because of His saying: "We will surely settle them in lofty chambers (ghurafan) of Paradise" (al-Ankabut: 58). Al-A'mash and Hamzah read "fi al-ghurfah" in the singular.

"And those who strive (yas'awna): they work against Our verses, seeking to nullify Our proofs and Our Book, and (mu'ajizin: as opponents, obstinate ones), thinking that they can escape Us by themselves and outpace Us. Those will be brought forth to the punishment." Say: "Indeed my Lord extends provision to whom He wills of His servants and restricts it for him. And whatever you spend of anything, He will replace it." Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: what is spent without extravagance or stinginess, "He will replace it." Al-Kalbi said: whatever charity you give and whatever you spend in goodness and piety, "He will replace it," either by hastening it to you in this world or by storing it up for you in the Hereafter.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn informed me, saying: Ahmad ibn Ja'far ibn Hamdan ibn Abdullah narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Dawud al-Qantari narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: al-Layth ibn Sa'd narrated to us, from Amr ibn al-Harith, from Abu Yunus, mawla of Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of God (ﷺ), that he said: "Indeed, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said to me: 'Spend, and I will spend upon you.'" [Fath al-Bari: 9/411; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 6/240.]

And Abdullah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Ibn Shadhan informed us, from Ja'unah ibn Muhammad, saying: Salih ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Sulayman ibn Amr, from Ibn Hazm, from Anas ibn Malik, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Every night a caller calls out: 'Build for death!' and a caller calls out: 'Build for ruin!' A caller calls out: 'O Allah, give the one who spends a replacement!' and a caller calls out: 'O Allah, give the one who withholds destruction!' A caller calls out: 'Would that people had not been created!' and a caller calls out: 'Would that, when they were created, they had reflected on what they were created for!'" [Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 8/222.]

He said: "I heard Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, say: 'Whatever you spend of anything, He will replace it.'"

"And He is the best of providers."

Abu Sufyan al-Thaqafi informed me, saying: al-Fadl ibn al-Fadl al-Kindi narrated to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn Dawud al-Khashshab narrated to us, saying: Suwayd ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Hamid ibn al-Hasan narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Every act of goodness is charity. Abd al-Hamid said: I asked Muhammad: "What is the meaning of 'what a man uses to protect his honour'?" He said: "Giving to a poet, or to one whose tongue is feared."

Mujahid said: If there is something in the hand of one of you, let him be moderate, and let him not interpret this verse, "Whatever you spend of anything, He will replace it," as a license, for provision is apportioned; perhaps his provision is little while he spends as one who is wealthy. The meaning of the verse is: "Whatever is from a replacement, it is from Him." A person may spend all his wealth in good, and then remain in need until he dies; but whatever replacement there is, it is from Him. The evidence for Mujahid's interpretation is what:

Abu Sufyan al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Bushayr narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Abi al-Khusayb informed me, saying: Mu'adh ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Amr ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ibn Allanah, that is Muhammad, narrated to us, from al-Awza'i, from Ibn Abi Musa, from Abu Umamah, who said: "You interpret this verse other than its true interpretation: 'Whatever you spend of anything, He will replace it.'"

And I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say, and otherwise may I be silent: "Beware of extravagance in wealth and spending, and hold to moderation, for no people ever became poor who were moderate."

And he (peace be upon him) said: "No one who is moderate ever suffered want." [Musnad Ahmad: 1/447.]

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Musa ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim al-Baghawi narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Hanbal narrated to us, saying: Asim ibn Khalid narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr informed me, saying: Hamzah narrated to us, from Abu al-Darda', from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Part of a man's understanding is gentleness in his livelihood." [Majma' al-Zawa'id: 4/74.]

"And He is the best of providers." The use of the plural (al-raziqin) is permissible because it is said: "The sultan provides for (razaqa) the soldiers," and "So-and-so provides for his dependents," as if He said: "He is the best of those who give."

"And on the Day when He gathers them all together, He will say to the angels: 'Did these people used to worship you?'" That is, these disbelievers. Al-Baqir said: it means the sword.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn informed me, from Abdullah ibn Ibrahim ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn Imran ibn Harun, from Sufyan ibn Waki', from Ibn 'Uyaynah, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, from Abu Ma'mar, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said:

The Prophet (ﷺ) entered Makkah while there were three hundred and sixty idols around the House. He began striking them with a stick he had, saying: ﴿The truth has come and falsehood has vanished; indeed falsehood is ever bound to vanish﴾ [al-Isra' 17:81]. ﴿The truth has come, and falsehood can neither originate nor restore.﴾

Say: "If I go astray, I only go astray to my own detriment, and I bear the consequence of my error; and if I am guided, it is by what my Lord reveals to me. Indeed, He is All-Hearing, Ever-Near."

﴿If only you could see when they are terrified, but there will be no escape﴾ — meaning from the punishment of this world, so there will be no deliverance — ﴿and they will be seized from a near place﴾ — meaning the punishment of this world. Al-Dahhak and Zayd ibn Aslam said: it is the Day of Badr. Al-Kalbi said: from beneath their feet.

Muhammad ibn Nu'aym informed us, from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Affan, from al-Hasan ibn Atiyyah, from Ya'qub al-Isfahani, from Ibn Abza, regarding ﴿If only you could see when they are terrified, but there will be no escape﴾, he said: it refers to being swallowed up in the desert (al-Bayda').

Aqil ibn Muhammad informed me that al-Mu'afa ibn Zakariyya al-Baghdadi informed them, saying: Muhammad ibn Jarir informed us, saying: Usam ibn Rawwad ibn al-Jarrah told me, saying: My father told us, saying: Sufyan ibn Sa'id told us, saying:

Mansur ibn al-Mu'tamir told us, from Rib'i ibn Khirash, who said: I heard Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, mentioning a trial that will occur between the peoples of the East and the West: "While they are in that state, the Sufyani will emerge at them from the dry valley, in the midst of that turmoil, until he descends upon Damascus. He will send two armies: one army to the East and another army to Madinah. They will descend in the land of Babel, in the cursed city and the wicked place, and they will kill more than three thousand people there, and they will rip open more than a hundred women there, and they will kill three hundred young men of the sons of al-Abbas there. Then they will move on to Kufa and ruin what is around it. Then they will set out heading for Syria, and a banner of guidance will come out from Kufa and overtake that army two nights later, and they will kill them, and not a single messenger from them will escape. They will rescue what is in their hands of captives and spoils. And his second army will come to Madinah and plunder it for three days and nights. Then they will set out heading for Makkah, and when they are in the desert (al-Bayda'), Allah the Mighty and Majestic will send Jibril (peace be upon him), who will say: 'O Jibril, go and annihilate them!' Qatadah said: that is when they come out of their graves. Ibn Mu'aqqil said: when they witness the punishment of Allah on the Day of Resurrection. ﴿They will be seized from a near place﴾ because wherever they are, they are near to Allah, not distant from Him, nor can they escape Him.

﴿And they will say﴾ when they witness the punishment in this world and the Hereafter, at the time of severity: ﴿We have believed in Him.﴾ ﴿But how can they reach (al-tanawush)?﴾ — from where can they obtain the repentance and the attainment of what they wish?

Ibn 'Abbas said: they ask for a return, but the time of return has not come. Abu 'Amr, al-A'mash, Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Khalaf read (al-tana'ush) with a hamzah and a long vowel, meaning delay and distance. It is said: "tanashaytu al-shay'" meaning I took it from afar, and al-nays is a slow thing.

The poet said:

He wished for a delayed (nay'ish) return that he might obey me, but after matters have happened, other matters have occurred.

Another said:

I came late (nay'ish) after it, and the news overtook me.

The rest read it without hamzah, from "tanawul" (reaching). It is said: "nashahu nawshan" when one reaches it.

The rajiz said:

"They reach (tanush) the basin, reaching (nawshan) from above, reaching with it the lengths of the wilderness."

"Tanawash al-qawm fi al-harb" means when some of them reach others and draw close. Abu 'Ubayd preferred omitting the hamzah, because its meaning is reaching, whereas with hamzah it means distance. How then could it say: "How can they reach from a far place" — from the Hereafter? How can they grasp repentance, when repentance is accepted only in this world, and this world has gone and become distant from the Hereafter?
